purpose: Prepare a dispute for a human decision-maker or representative: read the papers, establish what is said and by whom, find and check the law, and assemble a source-linked analysis. Stops before any decision.

steps.description: Confirm who, what law, which sources and which reviewer before anything runs.
Read every registered document into locatable passages.
Account for every document: read, or explicitly waived by a person.
Take factual statements word for word from the documents.
Identify the questions in dispute and attach the facts that bear on them.
Map evidence to issues; note gaps and statements that may conflict.
Search approved sources; list every authority the parties cite.
Confirm each cited authority exists in an approved source.
Confirm each authority is still good law, independently of who cited it.
Confirm each authority says what it is quoted as saying.
Confirm every finding points at unchanged source text.
Hold every finding that lacks a required passing check, and everything relying on it.
Set out the arguments open to each party, from verified findings only.
Assemble the source-linked report from verified findings.
Verify the audit chain and its completeness; confirm no hold is open.
A named reviewer approves, rejects or returns the report.
Fix the exact approved report version and its recipients.
A person confirms each recipient is entitled to receive it.
Stage the approved report for delivery; nothing is sent autonomously.
